abstract: Caenorhabditis briggsae is a widely used model for comparative genetic studies involving C. elegans. Genetic analysis in C. briggsae depends on mutations with clear, easily recognizable phenotypes, yet most mutants reported so far have been mentioned only as names and linkage groups, without underlying experimental data. This study reports 183 C. briggsae mutants belonging to 11 phenotypic classes, which represent the most comprehensive collection to date. Almost all mutants were recovered in EMS screens of the reference strain AF16. Our analysis revealed that 121 mutations define 55 loci and 62 remain unassigned. A combination of complementation tests, linkage tests, two- and three-factor crosses, and polymorphism-based mappings helped place 51 loci and 15 further mutations to the six linkage groups. We report the supporting data, map distances, linkage groups, and corrections to several earlier assignments. Twenty-three loci correspond to molecularly identified orthologs of C. elegans genes, including six for which we report genetic, rescue, or sequence evidence here. The levamisole-resistant mutants fall into at least three complementation groups, two of which correspond to Cbr-unc-38 and Cbr-unc-29 (levamisole-sensitive nicotinic acetylcholine receptor a and non-a subunit, respectively). Transgene rescue experiments identify Cbr-dpy-1 (mucin-like), Cbr-sma-6 (TGFb type receptor kinase), and Cbr-unc-4 (homeodomain transcription factor), genes that have long been in use as genetic markers. In all cases, molecularly identified genes are located on the same chromosome as their C. elegans orthologs, although gene order within chromosomes differs. The strains, map, and underlying data provide a resource for genetic and comparative studies in Caenorhabditis nematodes.
